geometry.note: Published coordinate from the LHAASO Collaboration's own peer-reviewed Chinese Physics C paper, confirmed verbatim on two separate mirrors (iopscience.iop.org and cpc.ihep.ac.cn) on 2026-09-21. It replaces an earlier OpenStreetMap/Nominatim rest-area geocode (precision 5000 m) that lies 3253 m away: inside its own claimed accuracy, but far coarser than this figure. Confidence is 'verified' because the coordinate comes from a journal article. The quoted arc-second figure implies sub-metre nominal precision, but accuracy is kept at 50 m as an allowance, since the quote describes the observatory's general Mt. Haizi location, not a specific surveyed structure corner.
geometry.quote: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) (Fig. 1) is located at Mt. Haizi (4410 m a.s.l., 600 g/cm2, 29°21'27.56"N, 100°08'19.66"E) in Daocheng, Sichuan province, P.R. China.

method: Published coordinate (29d21'27.56"N, 100d08'19.66"E) from the LHAASO Collaboration's own Chinese Physics C paper (doi:10.1088/1674-1137/ac3fa6), converted from DMS to decimal degrees. It supersedes the earlier OpenStreetMap/Nominatim rest-area geocode reused verbatim from the LHAASO site record (precision 5000 m): that point sat 3253 m away, inside its own claimed accuracy but far coarser than this published figure. The LHAASO Science Book (arXiv:1905.02773) could not be retrieved by any means tried (checked 2026-09-21); this independent Chinese Physics C paper was used instead. KM2A is independently sourced as circular (radius ~575 m core, ~635 m outer guard ring) and WCDA as 78,000 m2 (two 150x150 m pools plus one 300x110 m pool); this 50 m anchor is well under either shape's own size, but neither is drawn because no source consulted states its orientation or offset from this point.
name: LHAASO (reference point)
notes: KM2A (circular, ~575-635 m radius) and WCDA (78,000 m2, two 150x150 m pools plus one 300x110 m pool) are described with enough shape and size detail to draw, and this point's accuracy is well under either shape's own size, but no source consulted states their offset or orientation from this reference point, so neither is drawn.

summary.plain: The high-altitude LHAASO cosmic-ray and gamma-ray observatory on Haizi Mountain, Sichuan, shown here as a single published reference point.
